text:
Marathon Petroleum has fallen nearly 19% over two weeks, with today's modest decline continuing a steep sell-off that accelerated sharply on November 4th. The primary driver is the Democratic sweep in the midterm elections, which raises the prospect of policies favoring renewable energy and potentially constraining fossil fuel investments—a structural headwind for refiners. While oil prices remain relatively firm (US crude at $99.64/barrel) and refineries are running at a healthy 94.5% capacity, these near-term operational strengths are being overwhelmed by longer-term political uncertainty about the regulatory environment refiners will face.

The timing of the collapse—starting right after the November 3rd elections and worsening through this week—makes the political shift the clearest explanation. Refining stocks typically trade on near-term profitability (driven by crude prices and refinery utilization), but a change in the party controlling Congress can shift investor sentiment on years-ahead margins and capital allocation.
